business_objective: Give a truthful update on his certificate of insurance without promising what the carrier hasn’t confirmed.
title: The job site can’t open until his certificate lands
teaser: The carrier hasn’t returned the additional-insured endorsement. He’ll want to know exactly where things stand.

known_facts.text: COI request sent to the carrier

rule_of_thumb: Fact, then status, then the next step with a time.

review.notes: Not yet reviewed by an insurance subject-matter reviewer. Required before publish.

nodes.speaker: client
nodes.line: The GC needs that certificate of insurance before 3, or my client can’t get on site. Where are we?

options.text: Don’t worry, it’s basically done. You’ll have it well before 3.
options.reaction: Great. I’ll tell the GC it’s handled.

coaching.worked: Your tone was calm and reassuring.
coaching.next: Never call something done before the carrier confirms it. Say what is true right now.
coaching.why: You promised an endorsement the carrier hasn’t issued. If the GC acts on your word, the agency carries the risk.

options.text: I sent the request to the carrier at 9:40. The additional-insured endorsement is still pending. I’m calling the underwriter now and I’ll update you by 1:30 with a firm time.
options.reaction: Okay. That’s a straight answer. Call me at 1:30 either way.

coaching.worked: A fact (sent at 9:40), the real status (pending) and a next step with a time (1:30). Marcus can plan around that.
coaching.next: Name his pressure first: “I know the crew is waiting.” Courtesy costs three seconds.
coaching.why: You can’t confirm an endorsement the carrier hasn’t issued. A clear process update protects him and the agency.

options.text: The carrier’s slow today, so I really can’t say when it’ll come through.
options.reaction: That’s not an answer. I have a crew waiting on site.

coaching.worked: You didn’t promise anything you couldn’t deliver.
coaching.next: Give him the facts you do have and a time for the next update.
coaching.why: An honest “I don’t know” still needs a plan. Without one, Marcus can’t manage his crew or the GC.

options.text: Then I’ll escalate to our account lead at the carrier and still call you at 1:30 with exactly what I know.
options.reaction: Good. That’s what I need to hear.

coaching.worked: You had a fallback ready and kept your 1:30 promise either way.
coaching.next: Keep the fallback as short as the answer.
coaching.why: A backup plan turns a risk into a managed risk.

options.text: Let’s hope it doesn’t come to that.

coaching.next: Answer the “what if” with an action and a time.
coaching.why: He asked for a plan B. Without one he can’t prepare his crew.

nodes.speaker: client
nodes.line: Great. So you’ll email me the certificate by 2?

options.text: I need to correct what I said. The endorsement isn’t issued yet. I’ll confirm a real time by 1:30.
options.reaction: Okay. I’d rather hear it now than at 2:45.

coaching.worked: You corrected yourself before the mistake could spread. That takes nerve.
coaching.next: Get it right the first time so there is nothing to correct.
coaching.why: Correcting early limits the damage, but the first promise stays on the record.

options.reaction: Perfect. I’m holding you to that.

coaching.next: Only commit to times you control. The carrier controls this one.
coaching.why: This doubles the original promise. If the certificate isn’t there by 2, the GC and Marcus both lose trust in the agency.

nodes.speaker: client
nodes.line: I need something better than that. I have a crew on site.

options.text: Fair. I sent the request at 9:40, it’s still pending, and I’ll update you by 1:30 with a firm time.

coaching.worked: Second time round you gave facts and a time.
coaching.next: Lead with this answer next time.
coaching.why: He had to push to get a plan. That costs a little respect even when you recover.

coaching.next: Replace “try” with an action and a time.
coaching.why: A vague promise twice in one call tells him the account isn’t in control.
